title: Schema-Validated MCP Tool Server
description: Implement a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing at least three real tools with strict input/output schemas, deterministic validation errors, streaming-safe calls, and a conformance test suite that a reviewer can run in one command.
learningObjectives: Expose tools that validate inputs against strict schemas
Return deterministic, typed errors instead of stack traces
Handle concurrent and streaming tool calls correctly
Write a conformance suite an external agent can pass

milestones.title: Three real tools
milestones.objective: Implement three tools (e.g. text stats, file search within a sandboxed root, unit conversion) with JSON-schema validation.

milestones.title: Deterministic error contract
milestones.objective: All validation failures return typed, documented error codes — never raw exceptions.
milestones.expectedOutput: Error table documented and enforced by tests.

milestones.title: Parallel/streaming calls
milestones.objective: Support concurrent tool invocations without cross-request state leakage.
milestones.expectedOutput: Concurrency test with multiple simultaneous calls.

milestones.title: Conformance suite
milestones.objective: One command runs a suite any MCP client can be verified against (handshake, list, call, error paths).
milestones.expectedOutput: Suite documented in README with expected output.

categories.minimumExpectation: Invalid inputs never crash the server

categories.excellentExpectation: Security section documenting the threat model

constraints: No secrets or credentials in tools
Filesystem access limited to an explicit sandbox root
hints: Write the conformance suite first as a spec, then make the tools pass it — this is how real protocol implementations behave
